summary: In four isolated volatile-fixture cases, a known transport failure and unknown outcome released after /login became current rendered feedback on the current login form. A same-route known failure also remained visible after navigation to login, and a late-success control displayed success feedback there as well. This supports route-global outcome feedback, but does not establish that it is a defect; no auth lockout or context overwrite was shown. Login local validation worked, registrationCalls stayed at one per case, and generated passwords were absent from retained state/runtime/Parts/storage. No product changes or browser claims.

execution.scope: local fixture provider + actual createServiceRuntime/createPublicController/renderPublicSite tree; no browser, mounted-browser reachability unverified
execution.retained_credentials: generated password absent from retained controller state, runtime inspection, serialized PxC Parts and volatile storage; synthetic email is nonsecret identity

phase_qualification.note: The script's requestStatus and outcomeKind fields are sampled after the separate invalid-login local-validation control, so they describe that control (failed/validation-error), not registration completion.
phase_qualification.registration_completion_evidence: result and completedRoute.feedback in each observation
phase_qualification.automatic_registration_replay: none observed; registrationCalls remained exactly 1 after login validation in every case

limits: Feedback appearing on login is an observation, not proof of a product defect; success feedback appears there too, consistent with global outcome projection.
No real provider, backend, account, network write, browser, production authority, auth lockout, or context overwrite was exercised or established.
No PageRouter source/test change, commit, push, or publication.
